name: Geuel
title: The Spy from the Tribe of Gad
summary: Geuel, son of Machi, was the representative from the tribe of Gad among the twelve spies that Moses sent to explore the land of Canaan. He was one of the ten spies who returned with a negative report and advised against entering the Promised Land.
relatedPersons: Shammua son of Zaccur, spy from the tribe of Reuben

keyEvents.title: Chosen as a Spy
keyEvents.description: Geuel, son of Machi, was chosen by Moses to represent the tribe of Gad among the twelve spies sent to explore the land of Canaan.

keyEvents.title: Sent Out to Spy Out Canaan
keyEvents.description: Moses sent Geuel and the other eleven spies from the wilderness of Paran to investigate the land, its people, cities, and resources.

keyEvents.title: Exploring the Land of Canaan
keyEvents.description: Geuel and the other spies spent forty days exploring the land from the wilderness of Zin to Rehob near Lebo-Hamath.

keyEvents.title: The Negative Report
keyEvents.description: After returning, Geuel and nine of the other spies reported that the land was inhabited by powerful people and large fortified cities, spreading fear among the Israelites.

keyEvents.title: The People's Rebellion and God's Judgment
keyEvents.description: As a result of the negative report from Geuel and the other spies, the Israelites refused to enter the Promised Land. God judged that generation to wander in the wilderness for forty years.

keyEvents.title: Death of the Spies by Plague
keyEvents.description: The ten spies who brought the negative report, including Geuel, died of a plague before the Lord as punishment for causing the people to grumble against God.
